title: Introduce temporal RBAC leases, region-lock enforcement, and KMS affinity adapter
author: Marisol Vega
description:
Motivation: Customers asked for tighter, auditable short-lived operator grants and stronger data-residency enforcement that ties KMS selection to RBAC decisions. This PR implements three coordinated pieces: (1) temporal RBAC leases (time-windowed grants) for operator/automation workflows, (2) a region-lock enforcement middleware that validates per-request residency constraints and rejects or routes requests when tenants request region-locked handling, and (3) a KMS affinity adapter that maps RBAC + residency assertions to a prioritized KMS-provider list with safe fallback semantics.

Design summary: The temporal RBAC leases are expressed as a new optional claim in RBAC v2 bindings: "lease_window": {"not_before":"ISO8601","not_after":"ISO8601"}. The policy engine validates these at decision-time and records lease IDs in the audit envelope. Region-lock enforcement is a middleware added at the API ingress and the private control-plane egress; it checks the tenant's residency profile and an incoming "x-redwood-region-assertion" header. If the header conflicts with the tenant's locked region, the request is rejected with 403 and an audit tag. The KMS affinity adapter lives in pkg/kms/affinity and implements a deterministic provider selection algorithm that prefers in-region CMKs, then tenant-owned external providers, then a configured platform fallback. It produces a proof bundle attached to the encrypted payload metadata so downstream auditors can verify key choice.

Implementation notes: - Policy engine: added lease parsing and validation in pkg/auth/rbacv2/engine.go; leases are evaluated using the same evaluation cache to avoid perf regression. - Middleware: pkg/http/middleware/region_lock.go enforces region pin semantics; it integrates with the tenant profile cache and will short-circuit when tenants are in 'regional-exempt' mode. - KMS adapter: pkg/kms/affinity/adapter.go implements selection + proof bundling. The adapter exposes a small interface for callers: GetKeyForOperation(ctx, tenantID, resourceTags) -> {provider_id, key_id, proof_blob}. - Auditing: pkg/audit/writer/lease_audit.go records lease usage, proof blobs and region decisions into the immutable audit envelope. Audit entries include a SHA256 fingerprint of the lease and key selection for tamper-evidence.

Backward-compatibility and migration: New RBAC bindings are additive. Existing bindings without lease_window behave as before. The region-lock middleware is opt-in behind a feature-flag (features.region_lock=true) and a tenant-level flag (tenant.profile.region_lock=true) so we can stage enablement. KMS adapter falls back to current behavior when no residency or affinity info is present, so there is no breaking change for customers not using region pinning.

Testing and CI: - Added unit tests for lease validation (tests/unit/rbac_lease_test.go) and KMS adapter selection heuristics (tests/unit/kms_affinity_test.go). - Integration tests simulate cross-region requests and validate audit envelopes (tests/integration/rbac_region_kms_test.go). - Ran private-installer smoke in a VM with a mock KMS provider (local-kms) to verify fallback and proof attachment.

Checklist: - [x] RBAC engine: lease parsing and evaluation - [x] HTTP middleware: region-lock enforcement - [x] KMS adapter and proof bundling - [x] Audit writer: lease/key fingerprints - [x] Unit & integration tests - [x] Docs: runbook and migration guide - [x] Feature-flag gating and tenant opt-in

Performance: We measured decision latency before/after on a sample load: median auth decision increased from 2.1ms to 2.4ms (lease checks hit cache). KMS adapter adds negligible CPU on hot path; key selection is cached per-tenant for 60s by default. We added telemetry counters to track fallback frequency and average selection latency.

Security considerations: Lease IDs are unique UUIDv7 and recorded in audit for non-repudiation. Proof blobs are HMAC-signed with a platform signing key to avoid tampering; they do not include plaintext key material. All new endpoints and RPCs respect existing RBAC checks.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature-flag. 2) Enable for internal tenants only for 1 week; monitor audit volume and fallback rates. 3) Open beta for select customers with residency needs. 4) Gradual default-on for new tenants after 60-day observation window.

Related: ENG-5342 (temporal grants), SEC-112 (residency/KMS hardening).

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Please add a clarifying comment about lease time resolution (we use milliseconds vs seconds) — otherwise LGTM.
Marisol Vega: Reply: Updated comment and added a small helper (leases.go) that normalizes to millis; also added test coverage for boundary conditions.

Marisol Vega: Reply: switched error responses to the standard /api/v1/errors schema and added tests in integration suite.

Daniel Kim: Approval: approved — please squash and merge after CI passes.
release_notes: Add time-bound RBAC leases, region-lock middleware, and a KMS affinity adapter that prioritizes in-region keys and records auditable selection proofs. Opt-in via feature-flag and tenant-level setting.
risk_assessment: Medium - introduces new decision-time checks and audit volume. Mitigations: feature-flag, tenant opt-in, caches, and fallback semantics. Unit and integration tests included.
test_summary: Unit tests: pass (lease validation + KMS adapter). Integration: pass (cross-region flows, audit verification). Manual private-installer smoke with mock KMS: pass.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag behind main flag; staged tenant opt-in; monitor fallback rate, audit size, and auth decision latency; revert by disabling flag if abnormal.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps selection proofs compact (SHA256 + metadata) to avoid inflating audit logs. Follow-up work: add tooling to index proof blobs for fast forensic queries.
